facts.statement: Sanshuiornis is an extinct genus of bird from the Middle Eocene of Guangdong Province in southern China.
facts.quote: Sanshuiornis (meaning "bird from Sanshui Basin") is an extinct genus of bird from Middle Eocene deposits of Guangdong Province, south China.

facts.statement: The genus is known from a single holotype, IVPP V18116, which consists of an articulated complete right leg and foot.
facts.quote: It is known from the holotype IVPP V18116 an articulated complete right leg and foot.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the black oil shales of the Huayong Formation in the Sanshui Basin near Foshan.
facts.quote: It was found from the black oil shales of the Huayong Formation of the Sanshui Basin, near Foshan.

facts.statement: Sanshuiornis was named by Min Wang, Gerald Mayr, Jiangyong Zhang, and Zhonghe Zhou in 2011, with the type species being Sanshuiornis zhangi.
facts.quote: It was first named by Min Wang, Gerald Mayr, Jiangyong Zhang and Zhonghe Zhou in 2011 and the type species is Sanshuiornis zhangi.

facts.statement: Sanshuiornis exhibits resemblances to birds in the order Ciconiiformes.
facts.quote: Sanshuiornis shows resemblances to some Ciconiiformes birds.

facts.statement: Sanshuiornis is classified within the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Aves, subclass Neornithes, and superorder Neognathae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Aves subclassis: Neornithes superordo: Neognathae genus: Sanshuiornis

facts.statement: Sanshuiornis lived during the Lutetian to Bartonian stages, between 48.07 and 37.71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Bartonian (48.07 to 37.71 million years ago)
